title: A visit remembers the vet who attended it
subtitle: Review guide for test-pr vs origin/main — assembled by /human-review, merge-base 39ceefc.
summary:
What it does. visits gains a nullable vet_id, so a visit can name the vet that attended it. The vet flows end to end: a dropdown on the add/edit visit forms, a column in both visit lists, a field on VisitDto, and a LEFT JOIN FETCH so listing visits does not turn into an N+1.

What I already fixed, from /code-review and /simplify (detail at the bottom) — backend tests green after all six:

  • Vet lookup out of the controller, onto the repository  VetRepository.java:24
  • Three vet tests were passing vacuously — now flush + clear  VisitTest.java:296
  • Vet dropdown opened blank  visit-add.component.ts:36
  • Em-dash rule out of two templates, into a pipe  vet-name.pipe.ts:8
  • e2e vet picker no longer positional  add-visit.dsl.ts:48
  • Dead Vet import  VisitRestController.java:13

What is left is genuinely yours — five calls, none of which I should make for you. The first one is a live 500.

findings.title: Local only: the working tree has addVisitToOwner stripped of its vet handling
findings.body: Not a defect in the change set — HEAD is intact. An uncommitted edit in the working tree removes four things from addVisitToOwner: the VetRepository import, the field, @Validated on the body, and the whole if (vetId != null) setVet(...) block — +1 −6. Because the Add Visit form posts to that owner-scoped endpoint (visit.service.ts:34), booking through the UI silently drops the vet as the tree stands now: a bare curl returns 201 with vetId: null, the e2e scenario is red, and the video narrates it.
findings.why: Listed so the red test and the video are not mistaken for a defect in the branch. git checkout -- petclinic-backend/src/main/java/victor/training/petclinic/rest/OwnerRestController.java restores it. Everything below is about the committed change.

snippets.caption: The handler the form actually calls — vetId never leaves the DTO.
Why this is the path that matters: the form posts owner-scoped, not to /api/visits.

findings.title: The new foreign key makes every seeded vet undeletable — DELETE /api/vets/{id} now returns 500
findings.body: vet_id INT REFERENCES vets (id) carries no ON DELETE clause, and nothing on the JPA side nulls it out: Visit is the owning side and Vet has no visits mapping. deleteVet just calls delete(vet), so Postgres raises a FK violation, which handleGeneralException turns into a 500. The backfill on line 8 assigns a vet to every seeded visit, so all six demo vets become undeletable the moment this migration runs.
findings.why: Your call: ON DELETE SET NULL on the constraint, or null the visits out in deleteVet. Either changes behaviour, and amending V9 in place will trip Flyway's checksum on any database that already ran it — which is why I left it. No test covers deleting a vet that has visits.

snippets.caption: The migration — no ON DELETE, and an unconditional backfill.
The delete path that now breaks.

findings.title: The backfill hardcodes vet ids 1–6 and has no WHERE
findings.body: UPDATE visits SET vet_id = 1 + (id % 6) assumes vets holds exactly ids 1..6 — true only for a pristine V3 seed. Delete a vet and add another through the existing API before upgrading, and the UPDATE points at a missing id: FK violation, Flyway marks V9 failed, and the backend refuses to boot until someone repairs it by hand. And the comment above it ("every visit in the DB at this point comes from the V3 sample data") is false for any database that has been in use: visits created through the UI or booked over MCP silently acquire a fabricated attending vet.
findings.why: The commit's own design says a null vet is legitimate, and both the UI and the tests already render the — fallback — so this write buys a demo nicety at the price of a data-integrity assumption. House precedent (V5__clear_demo_owner_phone.sql) keys data fixes off a name, not a hardcoded id.

findings.title: PUT /api/visits/{id} silently clears the attending vet when vetId is absent
findings.body: The handler overwrites unconditionally, so an existing consumer that PUTs only {date, description} — a script, or a client generated from the OpenAPI spec before this change — now also wipes vet_id, with nothing in the response to say so. update_clearsTheAttendingVet blesses this as intended behaviour, which makes it a decision rather than a bug.
findings.why: Either document it as a breaking change to the endpoint, or distinguish "field absent" from "explicitly null" (a JsonNullable/PATCH split). Both are contract decisions.

snippets.caption: Absent vetId and explicit null are indistinguishable here.

findings.title: An unknown vetId answers 404, not 400
findings.body: getByIdOrNull throws a bare NoSuchElementException, which the advice maps to 404 with a plain-text "Not found!" body — not the ProblemDetail shape every other error uses. PUT /api/visits/5 with {"vetId": 999} on an existing visit 5 therefore returns a 404 that is indistinguishable from "visit 5 does not exist", and the Angular error handler surfaces the wrong message. A bad request field is a 400.
findings.why: Fixing it means picking an exception type and touching ExceptionControllerAdvice — a cross-cutting contract change, so it is yours. It applies to POST /api/visits too.

snippets.caption: The lookup I extracted — the null rule is now in one place, but the failure mode is still 404.

findings.title: @ManyToOne defaults to EAGER, so vets load on every visit-reading path
findings.body: Only findAllWithPetAndOwner got the LEFT JOIN FETCH v.vet. GET /api/pets, the owner-detail page and MCP list_visits each now issue extra SELECT … FROM vets when visits are materialised. The first-level cache bounds it to the number of distinct vets per session, so the cost is modest.
findings.why: I left it because fetch = LAZY risks a LazyInitializationException in the mappers that run outside a transaction — which is a correctness change disguised as a tuning knob, and needs your read on the other paths.

findings.title: Unrelated: the trace-window store races itself and drops a diagram
findings.body: trace-window-store.ts:13 read-modify-writes a shared JSON file from parallel Playwright workers; on the first traced run one worker read a truncated file and the scenario failed with SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input, losing its sequence diagram. Re-running with --workers=1 produced all four. Pre-existing, not this branch — but it will keep costing diagrams.
findings.why: Not fixed: it is outside the change set under review.

diagrams.title: Diagram deltas
diagrams.body: Red = added, red struck-through = removed. Each image is the delta, not the snapshot — produced by scripts/puml-diff.sh origin/main, which diffs every changed .puml and dispatches structural diagrams to puml_diff.py and sequence diagrams to seq_puml_diff.py. The sequence arrows now carry the real SQL and the request/response payloads, and the browser's page-load resource fetches are gone — that engine came in with the merge of origin/main.

notes.DB: One nullable FK column and one relationship: visits.vet_id → vets.id. Nothing else in the schema moved.
notes.DomainModel: Vet 1 — 0..* Visit. The multiplicity is the design statement: a visit may have a vet, which is what makes the change backward-compatible with the legacy rows.
notes.add-visit.spec.ts.genseq: Red is what this branch adds to the trace. The new == Add a visit attended by a vet == section is the boundary crossing that matters: GET /api/vets to fill the dropdown, then the booking round-trip. Each section is one @generate_sequence test in the file — the links below open the test that produced it and the diagram source.

sections.title: Entry Point Complexity
sections.body:
Grey is what the entry point already cost; green is what this branch added (red would be what it removed). Both snapshots come from the same extractor — the baseline was produced by re-running it against the merge-base source — so every row is a real before/after, including the MCP tools.

The shape is worth noticing: the +1s are the paths that now resolve or format a vet, while every +3 is the same thing paid over and over — the vet block in VisitMapperImpl, on every entry point that maps a visit. GET /api/owners was already the most expensive flow in the app at 20 and this pushes it to 23, so the change makes the heaviest entry point heavier rather than creating a new hot spot. On the MCP side only list_visits moved (3 → 4); the other four tools are untouched.

sections.title: Core business logic
sections.body:
Three decisions carry the feature; everything else is plumbing.

1. The vet is optional, by design. Legacy rows and MCP-booked visits have none, so the column is nullable and the association un-required. This is what lets the change ship without a data migration for real clinics.

snippets.caption: 2. A visit points at its vet, not the other way round — Vet has no visits collection, which is why deleting a vet has no cascade to follow (see finding 1).
3. “No vet” is a first-class display state, not an empty cell. Extracted during this review from two templates that each spelled the rule out inline.

sections.title: Requirements
sections.body:
What the change set was supposed to do, and what pins each of it. The flag on every row below is not a claim in this file: scripts/test-changes.py reads the diff against the merge-base and decides, per test case, whether it is new, edited, deleted or untouched. This file only says which requirement a test belongs to.

🌐 End-to-end (Playwright)1 new

A real browser, the real API, the real database.

  • Add a visit attended by a vet — picks a vet in the dropdown and reads the name back off the owner's visit list. It is the scenario tagged @generate_sequence, so its own trace is the sequence diagram above.

🔌 API (Spring MockMvc)4 new

VisitTest drives the two write endpoints and the read-back, inside a transaction that is flushed and cleared so the assertion reaches the database.

  • Creating with a vet, exposing it on GET, changing it, and clearing it.

🧪 Component (Jasmine)2 new

Both visit tables, rendered against a fixture that carries one attended visit and one unattended one — so the em-dash fallback is asserted, not assumed.

⚠️ Migration and vet lifecyclenothing

No test at any level runs V9 against a database whose vet ids are not 1–6, and none deletes a vet that attended a visit. Those are the two requirements below that carry no list, and the two findings at the top of this page.

requirements.text: A visit may name the vet who attended it — and may legitimately name none. visits.vet_id is nullable and Visit.vet is an optional @ManyToOne, so legacy rows, and visits booked over MCP, stay valid. The field travels the whole way out to VisitDto and back in through both write endpoints.

The per-pet list on the owner detail page and the cross-owner list on /visits, both through the vetName pipe extracted during this review — so the two tables cannot drift apart on what “no vet” looks like.

tests.name: renders the attending vet, and a dash when none is assigned

requirements.text: Existing visits are backfilled with one of the six seeded vets, so the UI has something to show. UPDATE visits SET vet_id = 1 + (id % 6), unconditional, in V9. Nothing pins this: no test runs the migration against a database whose vet ids are not 1–6, which is why findings 2 and 3 are as easy to miss as they are.

A vet can still be deleted. The requirement nobody wrote down, and the one the new foreign key broke: DELETE /api/vets/{id} now answers 500 for every seeded vet. No test at any level covers it — the empty list under this requirement is the honest rendering of that.

sections.body: The scenario below is the one carrying @generate_sequence: it is the only test that crosses every boundary this change touches, so its trace becomes the sequence diagram above. It is red right now — see finding 1.

The clearing behaviour that finding 3 asks you to confirm is intended — note the flushAndClear() I added, without which this assertion read back the controller's own in-memory instance and would have passed even with the save() deleted.

sections.title: What is not covered
sections.body:
• Deleting a vet that attended a visit — no test at any level, and it is currently a 500 (finding 1).
  • An unknown vetId — no test pins the status code, which is why finding 4 is easy to get wrong either way.
  • The V9 backfill — no test runs it against a database whose vet ids are not 1–6.
  • Three sequence diagrams changed only as regeneration artifacts (add-a-follow-up-visit…, add-a-visit-to-an-existing-pet…, emptying-the-last-name-field…): the red in them is Hibernate statement-label granularity, not behaviour. They are in review/assets/diagrams/ if you want to check that claim.

sections.title: Fixed for you
sections.body:
Everything below came out of /code-review and /simplify and had exactly one defensible answer, so I applied it rather than spending your attention on it. Backend tests are green after these. Anything needing a judgement call went to Look here first instead.

1. The vet lookup had two homes

VisitRestController carried a private resolveVet that both of its write paths called. The null rule — "no vetId means no vet, an unknown one is rejected" — is a property of looking a vet up, not of a controller, so it moved onto the repository. Spring Data enforces @NonNullApi on repository methods, so the parameter needed an explicit @Nullable: without it the call throws before it reaches the body, and three tests went red on the first run.

{{snippet:petclinic-backend/src/main/java/victor/training/petclinic/repository/VetRepository.java:18-29|The rule, now in one place.}}

2. Three tests were green for the wrong reason

VisitTest is @Transactional, so the test and the MockMvc-invoked controller share one persistence context. Every vet test asserted against the very instance the controller had just mutated in memory — they would have stayed green with visitRepository.save() deleted outright. They now flush and clear first, so the assertion reads the database.

{{snippet:petclinic-backend/src/test/java/victor/training/petclinic/rest/VisitTest.java:293-303|Added, and called before every read-back.}}

3. The vet dropdown opened blank

Both forms started from this.visit = {} as Visit, leaving vetId undefined. The placeholder option binds to null, and undefined !== null for Angular's option lookup, so the select rendered with selectedIndex = -1 — empty — until the user touched it.

{{snippet:petclinic-frontend/src/app/visits/visit-add/visit-add.component.ts:36|Same one-line change in visit-edit.}}

4. The same em-dash rule, written out twice

visit.vetFirstName ? visit.vetFirstName + ' ' + visit.vetLastName : '—' was spelled out inline in both visit-list templates. "No vet" is a display decision the whole app should make the same way, so it became a pipe — which also gets a long ternary out of a template.

{{snippet:petclinic-frontend/src/app/visits/vet-name.pipe.ts:8-19|Declared and exported from VisitsModule; both templates now read {{ visit | vetName }}.}}

5. The e2e vet picker depended on the placeholder's position

It selected option.nth(1) — "index 0 is the placeholder" encoded as an incidental fact about the template. Reorder the options, or add a second placeholder, and an unrelated scenario fails confusingly. It now picks the first option that actually carries a vet id.

{{snippet:petclinic-test/src/add-visit.dsl.ts:44-57|}}

6. A dead import

VisitRestController stopped naming the Vet type once the lookup moved to the repository. Removed.

verdict.label: not yet mergeable
bullets: Feature design — sound. Nullable FK, one association, artifacts regenerated not hand-edited.
V9 — two defects that reach production behaviour.
DELETE /api/vets/{id} — HTTP 500 for all six seeded vets. A regression, not a gap.
Backfill on any DB whose vet ids aren't 1–6 — Flyway failure, backend won't boot.
Red e2e + vet-less video = an uncommitted local edit, not the branch. See finding 1.
